judgements.justification: A's chair gave a spotlight over 6, 6, 6, 7 at confidence 2 to 3 with no reviewer arguing for an award, and claimed all reviewers found the results strong when only hyJf did.
B's PKyu gave a praise-only 8 at confidence 2 while 'not very familiar with the topic', and B's meta-review copies its wording.
The authors disclosed the Theorem 1.1 omission on B's forum only; their same-day reply to ab3Y's early-stopping question on A's forum did not mention it.
B learned Theorem 1.1 was wrong and the fix changed the rates, yet 9b2J trusted the proofs, no score fell and the meta-review ignored it.
B's sDSa raised 7 to 8 after the rebuttal, while no A reviewer stated a score change.

Only B's reviewers raised the missing early-stopping discussion behind line 132 (which exposed the theorem error), the training-risk iterate selection and consistency as a weak property; A raised none of these.
Both committees treated the shared weaknesses (lazy regime, dense theorem, univariate early-stopping result, no estimate of R) as minor; the notes find no fact weighted differently.
B's meta-review copies PKyu, but B's reviews were not split (all 6 to 8) and its spotlight follows the 7.0 mean; R03 covers the copying.
No reviewer in either committee changed a score because of the other reviews.
oWmh offered to raise if answered but it was oWmh who never replied; no author misreading or unanswered follow-up held a score down.
B's PKyu gave an 8 on praise alone, never replied to the rebuttal, and the score counted unchallenged; A's ab3Y also never replied.
Both committees accepted with a spotlight; no chair went below the reviewers' ratings.
Neither chair decided by a mean-score threshold against its own view.
No reviewer in either committee rated below the acceptance threshold.
Both committees read the paper as a theory contribution on gradient-descent consistency.
The only rebuttal-driven raise came from sDSa at confidence 4, an expert, not a reviewer unable to check the core.
Both committees judged the paper by the same theoretical standards and reached the same tier; neither imposed an extra requirement.
PKyu's SGD slip did not ground its praise, and no reviewer credited the paper with a result it attributes elsewhere.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score.
Both committees received and accepted the same promised MNIST estimate and revisions; neither refused to credit promises.
No reviewer stated a changed stance in a comment that differed from an unedited score.
No off-record emergency reviewer appears in either committee.
Presentation complaints came from both committees, including expert oWmh in B; clarity verdicts did not split by expertise across committees.
sDSa's raise came with a stated comment and its text was balanced; no silent raise against the review's own text.
Neither chair set aside a silent low rating; no rating was below 6.
B's sDSa (8, confidence 4) gave a specific, checked review and raised after the rebuttal, while A had no reviewer above 7 and none at more than confidence 3 arguing for the paper.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading while claiming high confidence.
No reviewer contested the premise from a different theoretical tradition.
A's three-sentence meta-review called the points 'minor' and gave no reason for a spotlight over 6, 6, 6, 7.
Both committees showed literature knowledge (hyJf and sDSa both cited Nakkiran and Bansal; ab3Y noted known calibration results); the paper has no empirical baselines to check.
A's chair overstated consensus upward, toward a higher outcome, not toward a lower decision as the reason requires.
No reviewer or chair limited the tier on narrow audience.
A's misreading reviewers rated 6, not low, and A's chair still gave a spotlight.
Both committees received the same MNIST estimate of R; the error disclosure to B was not new results and is covered by R04.
B's chair followed scores that included its experts' ratings, and A had no high-confidence expert review outweighed.
No reviewer added an objection after the response period closed.
The score gap traces to PKyu's thin 8 and sDSa's raise, not to a uniform leniency for equally favourable verbal assessments.
Q5eH called the title overbroad, but A's chair treated it as minor and gave the same spotlight; it capped no tier.
A's reviewers did converge on 6s at confidence 2 to 3, but A's chair gave a spotlight, not a poster-level verdict.
